subject: Monthly vitals: latency / cost / uptime / usage — bridge & escalation plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: July monthly vitals — initial read & asks

Team,

Attached is the July monthly vitals packet (see 2026-07-monthly-vitals.pdf). High level notes up front: 
- Latency: P95 generation latency up ~12% MoM on hosted API, concentrated on long-context chat workloads (seq > 2k).
- Cost: token-processing CPU spend up ~9% (quantization rollout was partial; see section 3).
- Uptime: we saw a 22-min partial outage in eu-west-2 on 2026-07-03 during a control-plane rollout — impacting Dedicated customers on that region.
- Usage: two customers (one external, Acme Analytics) show sudden throughput bursts tied to a new internal pipeline.

As we prep for the QBR readout on 2026-07-22, I need the following before EOD Monday: 
1) Jasmine — annotated slide with proposed mitigation owners for latency and cost (1 slide).
2) Tessa — brief runbook for eu-west-2 rollback + postmortem draft.
3) Dylan — quick econometrics on the Acme spike and recommended throttling/burst policy.

Please reply with owners and ETA.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: July monthly vitals — initial read & asks

Thanks Markus — I have the slide in progress and will drop a draft in the Drive link by EOD Monday. Quick notes: 
- Latency: I agree this looks concentrated on long-context requests. My immediate proposal is a two-track mitigation: 1) fallback model variant (lower-context kernel) for requests >2k tokens; 2) adapt batching windows for long sequences. I will sketch tradeoffs on the slide.
- Cost: I can pull exact quantization rollout percentages per fleet; expect a ~3pp variance across Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Acme spike: loop in Dylan for telemetry; will reach out to their engineering contact to understand the pipeline.

Owners & ETA (preliminary):
- Slide: Jasmine (2026-07-12 17:00 PDT)
- Runbook draft: Tessa (2026-07-13 12:00 PDT)
- Acme triage: Dylan + Jasmine (2026-07-12 14:00 PDT)

I'll attach the latency raw export once I finish parsing (latency-deltas-raw.csv).

Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Head of Reliability Analytics
Redwood Inference
From: Rebecca Lang <rebecca@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:26:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: sudden throughput spikes — Acme context

Hi Jasmine, Dylan —

Thanks for the quick flag. We deployed a new batch enrichment pipeline on 2026-07-02 that parallelizes requests to your hosted API. We didn't expect the burst pattern — apologies.

Quick context: the job fans out many short requests and occasionally escalates to long-context aggregation in our postprocessing step. We're happy to coordinate throttles or backoff. If you can share a short-term token rate cap that won't break our downstream processing, we'll implement.

Rebecca
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Analytics

--
Attachment: acme-job-manifest.yaml (reference only)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: July monthly vitals — runbook + rollback plan

Hi all,

Draft runbook summary below (full doc in Drive). Key actions: 
- Immediate (0-1h): enable canary-block on control-plane rollout in eu-west-2, mitigate routing weight to fallback pool.
- Short (1-6h): re-route Dedicated customers in impacted subnet to alternative region (us-west-2) with traffic shaping; notify CS and affected accounts.
- Medium (6-72h): rollback the rollout artifacts and deploy a hotfix that patches the kernel selection for long-context sequences.

Risk notes: the rollback will temporarily increase token cost by ~5% while cache warms. We'll include that in the QBR slide.

I will attach the postmortem stub (region-eu-logs.zip) once logs are sanitized. ETA for full runbook and postmortem: 2026-07-13 12:00 PDT (on schedule).

Tessa
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly vitals: latency / cost / uptime / usage — bridge & escalation plan

Good progress team — this is the leadership update I'll read on Friday. Final asks before the QBR: 
1) Jasmine: consolidate the slide into two bullets for Exec (impact + mitigation + owner + ETA). Keep one backup slide with numbers.
2) Tessa: paste the immediate steps into the incident timeline (one-liner per hour).
3) Dylan: provide the Acme throttle recommendation (tokens/sec) and an estimated revenue impact if we limit bursts.
4) CS: notify Acme that we'll propose a short-term token cap and a follow-up architecture call. (Dylan please own).

Also note procurement pinged asking if we need a credits exception for Acme while they rework their pipeline (procurement@corptech.com). Laura wants a recommended credits allowance number if we elect to be conservative.

I'll stitch the art into the Exec slide deck Monday morning and circulate final deck for review.

Thanks — see you on the readout.

Laura
VP, Customer Success & Ops
Redwood Inference
